# vita-memio 1.6.0

Games load faster, above all their graphics data. If you are new to vita-memio, start with the [README](https://github.com/Osaul4ik/vita-memio#install): it explains the install step by step.

## In short

- **Much less waiting in games that read many tiny pieces.** Over a whole play session (all reads added up, in loading screens and while playing - not one loading screen), Catherine: Full Body waited about 86% less for the card than it would have without read ahead: 7 s instead of about 53 s in 87 s of play. GTA San Andreas waited about 58% less, GTA Vice City about 41% less. Games that jump around their files, such as Gravity Rush, gain little. The [README](https://github.com/Osaul4ik/vita-memio#how-much-faster) explains how this is measured and lists more games.
- **Faster than 1.5.1 in many commercial games,** for example Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA F 2nd and PCSB01007, which spend about 23% and 40% less time waiting per MiB read.
- **Safer restarts.** Restarting from VitaShell or HENkaku could sometimes end in an error at start that needed a hard reset. That is fixed.
- **A new Kernel memory choice** that needs less memory without slowing games down (it is the default).
- **A status window** with the version and the memory the plugin uses.

After updating, **switch your storage on again** in Settings (everything starts from the defaults).

**Tip:** vita-memio is recommended together with [vita_cpu_tweaks](https://github.com/devnoname120/vita_cpu_tweaks) by devnoname120. It switches on the Vita's hardware data prefetchers, which the firmware turns off at every start, so memory reads get faster - in games and in vita-memio's copies. The two plugins work side by side; install it as its page says.

## New

- **Repeated reads come from memory.** Many commercial games read the same graphics data again a moment later. vita-memio now keeps the latest such reads in memory and gives them to the game from there instead of reading the card again. There is nothing to set; it switches itself off in a game where it does not help. It works for commercial games only, not for homebrew, Adrenaline or the system's apps.
- **Read ahead understands more games.** It now also recognises games that read a file in big and small pieces in turn, or read again part of what they just read.
- **Kernel memory: Full / Medium / Low.** This replaces the old *Low kernel memory* switch.
  - **Medium** (640 KiB, the default): the SD2Vita and the memory card share one set of buffers. A game reads from one card at a time, so games are as fast as with *Full*.
  - **Full** (768 KiB): each storage its own buffers. A little faster only when you copy between the two cards.
  - **Low** (512 KiB): for consoles with many kernel plugins, if you see error **C1-2569-2**.
  - The change works after a restart.
  - I use **Full** myself, as my console has enough memory. **Medium** is the default because nobody can know how many other plugins you run.
- **Status window.** In **Settings → Devices → vita-memio**, press the *Driver: …* row: it shows the version, the status, how much kernel memory the plugin uses and how much is still free, and the storage driver.
- **HUD: DMA share.** The HUD now shows how much of the copying the DMA chip did. DMA near 100% is normal.
- **Tester: reads like games do them.** The tester can now read the way games do: overlapping, backwards, big and small pieces mixed, and reading the same data again.

## Fixed

- **Restart from VitaShell or HENkaku.** Before the console restarts or switches off, the plugin now puts every storage back the normal way, lets its reads finish and saves its files, so the cards are shut down cleanly.
- **Boot problems are easier to find.** While the console starts, the log and the safe-mode marker are written to the card at once, so they survive a hard reset.

## Changed

- **Adaptive learns every launch afresh** instead of remembering each game. It settles quickly, and if you go to the home screen and come back, it goes on where it was. `tuning.bin` now keeps only the measurements of your card and console.
- **Copy on the system core is simpler.** The *C + NC All* choice is gone: with *DMA copy* on, the DMA chip does almost all the copying anyway. Keep it at *C + NC R/A*.
- **R/A Test removed** from the overlay: *Adaptive* does this job by itself now.
- **Old files are not converted.** Settings, per-game overlay settings and `tuning.bin` from another version are deleted and the defaults used. Nothing breaks if you forget to delete the folders when updating.
- **Log:** more detail on how each game reads.

## Good to know

- **Error C1-2569-2** means the console is out of kernel memory. First close one of the open apps if two are running at once (for example VitaShell and Settings), or hide the HUD. If it still happens, set *Kernel memory* to *Low*. More in the [README](https://github.com/Osaul4ik/vita-memio#problems).
- **Verify transfers** is only for testing for errors; **Enable log** and **Statistics** are for measuring performance. Keep all three off for normal play.

## Update

1. Open **Settings → Devices → vita-memio** and switch **Driver** off.
2. Restart the console.
3. Unpack `vita-memio-1.6.0.zip` (or the `-more_logs` one) and replace `vitamemio_kernel.skprx`, `vitamemio_hud.skprx` and `vitamemio.suprx` in `ur0:tai/`. **Always replace all three together.**
4. Delete the folders `ur0:data/vita-memio/` and `ux0:data/vita-memio/`.
5. Restart the console.
6. Open **Settings → Devices → vita-memio** again and switch on the storage you use.

Your `config.txt` stays as it is. Deleting the folders resets the settings, the per-game overlay settings and the card measurements; the plugin measures your card again by itself while you play.

## Files

There are **two archives**. If unsure, take the first one.

- **`vita-memio-1.6.0.zip`** — the normal version, for everyone.
- **`vita-memio-1.6.0-more_logs.zip`** — the same plugin, but with *Enable log* on it also writes a detailed summary of each game's reads (how much came from the card, from read ahead, from memory). For people who measure performance or help with testing. Its version ends in `-more_logs`.

Each archive holds:

- `vitamemio_kernel.skprx`, `vitamemio_hud.skprx`, `vitamemio.suprx` — the plugin (all three go to `ur0:tai/`; always take all three from the **same** archive).
- `vitamemio_tester.vpk` — optional app that measures your card.
- `SHA256SUMS` — to check the downloaded files.

Tested on one console: a PCH-1000 on firmware 3.65. Back up your cards before installing, as with any plugin that touches storage.
